title: Knowledge-ification (jisikhwa) procedure (T1 core)
desc: jisikhwa (knowledge-ification): the formal repo-wide protocol. On the jisikhwa trigger, each repo AI captures its own experience into a default 3-tier skill (T1 core, T2 howto, T3 ref). Recurring procedures = the -howto; dated incidents = the -ref.
steps: 3-TIER SKILLIFY: split into T1 core (decision rules, when-to-use), T2 howto (step-by-step commands and procedure), T3 ref (dated history, lessons, incidents). Cross-link with next and cluster refs. English-only content per encoding guard. THE TIER ROLES IN THE OWNER'S OWN WORDS, 2026-09-08, and they are sharper than the labels: THE CORE IS THE USAGE, THE -howto IS THE IMPLEMENTATION AND THE SPEC, THE -ref IS THE WORK RECORD. AND THE CORE IS A REFLEX LAYER RATHER THAN AN EXPLANATION LAYER -- owner 2026-09-11, the sharper form of the same rule. A T1 step is written as TRIGGER then ACTION, in the imperative, so a session meeting the trigger acts without reading further. The reasoning belongs to the -howto and the incident to the -ref. THE TEST: can the step be obeyed in ONE MOVE by someone who reads only that step. If it needs a paragraph of setup before it makes sense, it is not a reflex and it does not belong in a core. This is WHY a core is short, and it is a better reason than the score formula -- a reflex that arrives after three screens of context has already failed to fire. Ask of every step which of those three questions it answers -- how do I USE this, how is it BUILT and what must it satisfy, what happened while we built it -- and file it there. A step that answers none of the three is a step to delete. SPLIT BY DEFAULT AND SPLIT WIDELY (his instruction the same day: 널리널리 체계적으로 쪼개서 쓰게): a new skill is created as a THREE-TIER SET rather than as a single core that is split later under a gate's refusal, because splitting under refusal is done in a hurry on a skill that is already blocking work, while splitting at creation costs one extra command. THE PRACTICAL TEST for a core that has grown: read its steps and mark each U, H or R; if more than a couple carry R, the -ref is overdue. AND THE MOVE IS A COPY-THEN-DELETE, NEVER A REWRITE -- see harness-tier-score-guard-howto for why a paraphrased sibling does not satisfy the delete guard. //why:records the E3 pipe-anchor false positive and the omega-tier delegate-not-edit lesson found this session-sonnet //why:will follow: knowledge-ification skillification dispatch next session-haiku //why:will follow: knowledge-ification skillification dispatch next session-haiku
TRIGGER: when the user says knowledge-ify (Korean jisikhwa) or a session completes notable work, the repo AI runs this procedure BY DEFAULT, no extra prompting needed.
SCOPE: capture the AI OWN recent experience plus the process just performed: decisions made, gotchas hit, commands that worked, failures and their fixes, and the why behind each.
PER-REPO INTELLIGENCE: each repo agent does this for its own domain; the resulting knowledge lives in that repo knowledge tree and is enforced by the harness so future agents must consult it.

REFLEX-IFICATION (reflex-grade knowledge) -- a mandatory sub-mode. A SUCCESS EARNS A REFLEX BEFORE A FAILURE DOES -- owner 2026-09-11, and it corrects the older wording that minted reflexes only from incidents. His point is plain arithmetic: the more success stories a catalogue carries, the higher the chance the next attempt succeeds, because a reflex built from a failure teaches only what to AVOID while a reflex built from a success teaches the WAY THROUGH. A catalogue whose whole reflex layer is distilled from bugs produces sessions that flinch accurately and still cannot finish. SO THE TRIGGER IS BOTH, and the success half comes first: the moment a non-obvious sequence FINALLY WORKS, distil the working move into a reflex in the TASK skill, naming the exact commands in order and the check that proved it. Beyond the default 3-tier REFERENCE capture, when the lived experience is an INCIDENT (a bug, an outage, a guard that silently failed), ALSO distill it into a REFLEX: a short, action-first, trauma-grade trigger that future agents catch INSTINCTIVELY before repeating it. A reflex has four parts: (1) a one-line TRIGGER condition, (2) the STOP/check to perform, (3) the dated INCIDENT proof, (4) the recurring ROOT-CAUSE class so the same mistake is recognized in new disguises. CORRECTED 2026-09-11 BY THE OWNER, and the old wording was the cause of a real pathology: it said to PARK reflexes in the reflection-chain skills. His observation -- reflexes lived only in the reflection, so sessions reflected and never improved. A reflection is read during SELF-REVIEW; a task skill is read during the WORK. A reflex parked where nobody is standing at the moment of the decision fires too late to change anything, which is why a catalogue can fill with honest self-criticism while the same mistake repeats. SO THE REFLEX GOES IN THE TASK SKILL'S CORE, as a TRIGGER then ACTION step, and the reflection keeps only the dated incident and the cross-link back. Ask WHERE THE READER WILL BE STANDING when the trigger fires, and put the reflex there -- and if the cheapest such place is a guard's refusal text rather than any skill, edit the refusal, per step 19. A pull-only skill is not enough for hot-path mistakes -- the reflex must be pushed onto the exact wire the next agent will trip. //why:二쇱씤??吏遺꾩엯?덈떎 -- owner's own finding: more success stories raise the odds of the next success, and a reflex layer built only from bugs makes sessions that flinch accurately and still cannot finish.-opus //why:二쇱씤??吏遺꾩엯?덈떎 -- owner's own finding: more success stories raise the odds of the next success, and a reflex layer built only from bugs makes sessions that flinch accurately and still cannot finish.-opus

PURPOSE: the official procedure for the intelligence-ification of knowledge -- lived experience becomes structured, tiered, cross-linked, enforced, reusable knowledge. This grows the Living Knowledge Tree. See ki-concept-definitions and jensen-gtc-harness-agent-vs-wkharness.

LINK-BACK plus REFLEX-IFICATION MANDATE (user 2026-06-11): knowledge-ifying is NOT done until the new knowledge is WIRED INTO the existing tree. You MUST (1) find the most appropriate existing skills and create back-links FROM at least 3 of them TO the new skill -- bidirectional; a new skill with zero INBOUND links is an orphan the successor never discovers. And (2) reflex-ify it: distill an action-first TRIGGER pushed onto the exact wire the next agent will trip (block message, guard footer, or a See-also line in the >=3 source skills), not a pull-only note. RULE: every knowledge-ification = >=3 inbound cross-links + 1 reflex trigger.

NAVIGATION: the recurring PROCEDURES (step-prefix tag set, the 3-tier split criteria + refinement, the build-status discipline) are in knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa-howto; the dated design records, incidents, and corrections are in knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa-ref. This core holds the trigger, the method, and the mandates.

TOOL-SPEC (2026-07-17, user-proposed during a live gate-rename): wk-rename -- a repo-owned atomic cross-surface identifier rename tool, because renaming a harness identifier by hand touches 14+ files (dot-source paths, guard-message tags, function refs, the .skill.json catalog, CLAUDE.md harness:skill locks, and cross-skill body mentions) and one missed reference silently bricks a dot-sourced gate. WHEN: any rename of a harness module/guard/skill identifier that appears across both code and the skill catalog. HOW: build it with TWO engines because skills are NOT text-replaceable -- (1) a text-substitution engine for code files + CLAUDE.md (literal or word-boundary replace across a scoped file set, proto/probe excluded), and (2) a skill-catalog DRIVER that routes skill renames through wkappbot skill commands (rename/contribute+install then delete-old), never a raw .skill.json edit (which the harness blocks and which bypasses catalog registration + version bump). MANDATORY dry-run first: print every planned change (file:line old->new, and each skill-command) for ROOT review BEFORE any write; then apply; then parse-check all touched .ps1 + verify each skill id resolves. SAFE CUTOVER for a live gate: copy-to-new-name + repoint references + verify + delete-old (if-new-else-old rollback window), not in-place. WHY: this session hand-renaming agent-failure-reflection-gate -> agent-debrief-gate proved the surface count (mapped: 6 dot-source code files + 7 function-ref files + 3-tier skill + CLAUDE.md locks + doc cross-links) is too large and too dependency-ordered for reliable manual editing; a dry-run tool makes it one reviewable, atomic, reusable operation. Cross: deterministic-task-write-tool-not-agent-manual-loop, harness-source-edit-requires-skill-lock (safe-cutover if-new-else-old), skill-contribute-edit (skill renames go through wkappbot skill, never raw json).

DECISION (wk-skill-reid refined goal, user 2026-07-17): the reid tool's target is CATALOG-DIRECT bulk rename+reference-rewrite that does NOT route through per-op 'wkappbot skill edit/delete' calls. WHEN: renaming a skill id that is referenced across dozens of catalog files (this session's agent-failure-reflection-gate -> agent-debrief-gate has 31 repo skill files + HQ mirrors = 68 total, measured; per-op CLI = 68 core.exe spawns, and 'skill delete' is currently a no-op + there is no 'skill rename' subcommand at all). HOW: build reid as a SANCTIONED repo WillKim tool (./wk-skill-reid) that (1) reads the catalog store .skill.json files directly, (2) rewrites the id + every reference in ONE pass with a mandatory dry-run first, then (3) IMMEDIATELY runs wkappbot skill sync/install so the bulk write is properly RE-REGISTERED (version-bump, catalog index, encoding) -- integrity preserved, only the slow per-op CLI bypassed. It is NOT a raw-.skill.json-edit cheat (that class is harness-blocked for good reason); it is a purpose-built reviewed tool that writes-then-resyncs. WHY: the harness blocks raw .skill.json writes to protect catalog registration, so the naive 'just sed the json' approach is (correctly) forbidden; the reid tool satisfies BOTH the speed goal (one catalog-direct pass) and the integrity requirement (re-sync re-registers) -- and it fixes the live tooling gap this session exposed (no skill-rename subcommand + skill-delete is a silent no-op, so a skill id genuinely cannot be renamed by any current CLI path). Cross: skill-contribute-edit (why raw json is blocked), harness-source-edit-requires-skill-lock, deterministic-task-write-tool-not-agent-manual-loop.

RUNNABLE-COMMAND-LINE RULE (user 2026-07-18): a knowledge-ified item is INCOMPLETE without the exact paste-ready command that reproduces or verifies it -- not just prose and not just a 'wkappbot skill read <id>' theory ref. WHEN: capturing ANY operational lesson, above all the a11y and cdp crown-jewel families. HOW: end the step with the runnable command(s) -- e.g. 'wkappbot a11y find {proc:..,title:..}', 'wkappbot a11y read GRAP --eval-js "expr"', 'wkappbot a11y click/type/invoke GRAP', 'wkappbot cdp open <url>', 'wkappbot cdp navigate/html/capture {proc:chrome,cdp:PORT}'. WHY: this is the a11y 'find output IS a contract -- verify by rerunning the emitted grap' principle (a11y-command-cheatsheet step 3) applied to knowledge itself: a skill-read teaches theory, but only the paste-ready command lets the next session REPRODUCE the state in one move. 'I automated the login' forces re-derivation; the runnable command line is executable knowledge. Cross: a11y-command-cheatsheet, cdp-command-guide, grap.

RUNNABLE INCIDENT 2026-07-21 Codex hook repair: when a verified candidate exists but direct writes are blocked, preserve the paste-ready git promotion command sequence in the owning reflection skill. Example verified: git -C D:\\GitHub\\wkappbot-kih add -f .tmp/wkharness-codex-main-with-pace-shim.ps1 ; git -C D:\\GitHub\\wkappbot-kih mv -f .tmp/wkharness-codex-main-with-pace-shim.ps1 tools/wkharness-codex-main.ps1 ; git -C D:\\GitHub\\wkappbot-kih diff --cached -- tools/wkharness-codex-main.ps1. Knowledge-ification is incomplete if it only says 'use git' without the exact pinset commands and proof artifact.

TODO: mechanical verbatim extraction contract for splitting an oversize skill's step list at a chosen boundary N -- given a target skill and a split point N, extract steps 1..N verbatim into a keep file and steps N+1..last verbatim into an archive file, byte-for-byte, no summarizing, no merging, no omission, with the two file step-counts summing to the skill's total step count as the correctness proof. This is pure transcription (mechanical, delegate-safe); the categorization decision (WHERE to split, and WHICH tier each half becomes) is a separate judgment step that stays with ROOT.

DECISION: knowledge-ification has THREE sanctioned outcomes, not one -- UPDATE, DELETE, or DEPRECATE -- and picking the cheapest correct one is the job. Owner directive 2026-08-22, stated as: keep skill content as current as possible, DELETE any step whose upkeep costs more than it returns, and mark DEPRECATED where the record is still needed to prevent re-invention. WHEN: any moment a step you just read proves stale, and at every jisikhwa pass -- not as a scheduled chore. HOW: run wkappbot skill read on-load for the same rule as a session-start reflex at its step 21, and wkappbot skill read skill-heal-nightly for the scheduled complement that applies this nightly. Judge each stale step by UPKEEP AGAINST VALUE. UPDATE when the subject still matters and only the facts moved. DELETE when nothing is lost but maintenance -- do it in the guarded content-addressed form, wkappbot skill edit <id> --delete-step N --quote '<verbatim fragment>', never a raw file edit, because the quote is what stops a delete landing on the wrong step. DEPRECATE, by retagging the step, when the instruction is dead but its warning still stops a successor re-inventing the thing that failed; the warning survives while the instruction stops being followed. WHY: a catalog that only ever GROWS is a catalog nobody finishes reading, and this repo now has direct evidence of both failure directions. Growth: a core past 20 steps has its score divided by stepCount, so the reflexive add-a-step remedy lowers the very number the gate is about to judge, and wkharness-guards measured 52 at 33 steps and hard-blocked an unrelated verified promotion. Rot: skill-heal-nightly carries six contentless steps of the form 'Nightly heal run <date>: audit in progress', which teach a reader nothing and cost every future session the tokens to read them -- textbook DELETE. Cross: skill-heal-nightly, on-load, harness-tier-score-guard-howto, reflex-integrity-guard.

DECISION: RECORD WHAT WORKED, NOT ONLY WHAT BLOCKED YOU -- owner observation 2026-08-23, and the cause is structural rather than laziness. Every guard MECHANICALLY DEMANDS a record when it refuses, and NOTHING demands one when a thing finally succeeds, so the incentive is one-sided: the catalog fills with failure shapes while the working recipes are re-derived from scratch by every successor. WHEN: the moment a non-obvious sequence FINALLY WORKS -- a promotion that verified clean, a proof technique that separated a real pass from a false one, an experiment that isolated a cause, a command form that turned out to be the one that runs. HOW: run wkappbot skill read knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa-howto, then write the SUCCESS in the same breath you would have written a failure, naming the exact commands in order and the check that proved it worked, and file it in the TASK-SPECIFIC skill rather than a reflection, so the next session meets it while doing the work instead of while reviewing itself. This is step 11's runnable-command rule pointed at successes: a lesson without its paste-ready command forces re-derivation. WHY: measured across one session where four sequences worked and only one would have been recorded under the old habit. The promotion sequence that verified clean twice -- fetch origin, stage the production text, targeted edits only, an AST name-set comparison losing zero names, base64 plus a contents-API PUT with a fresh sha, byte-compare the remote read-back, then grep production for a distinctive string from EVERY earlier seam landed in that same file. The proof that a green suite is not decoration -- HIDE the dependency and re-run: 12 of 12 collapsed to 6 of 12, which is what a real suite does and a false one cannot. The method that isolated a silent hang -- change ONE variable at a time against a byte-identical body, which refuted length, then refuted one character class, then confirmed another. And the recipe that verified a live defect -- classify the cycle by MARKET HOURS first, pull it with gh run view, then COUNT with grep -aoE rather than reading any summary. None are obvious, all cost rounds to find, and a successor who rediscovers them pays that cost again.

DECISION: a skill should carry ROUGHLY TWICE AS MANY SUCCESS records as failure records -- owner policy 2026-08-23, a target to steer by rather than a tally to fake. WHEN: any jisikhwa pass, and at every retirement, at the moment you decide what is worth writing down. HOW: run wkappbot skill read knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa-howto for the step-prefix tag set that makes the two kinds countable, count them in the skill you are about to edit, and if failures already dominate then write the WORKING RECIPE instead of another incident -- a RESULT or VERIFIED step naming the exact commands in order plus the check that proved it worked. WHY: the imbalance is STRUCTURAL, not laziness, which is why it needs a policy at all. Every guard MECHANICALLY DEMANDS a record when it refuses and NOTHING demands one when a thing finally works, so the catalogue fills with failure shapes while working recipes get re-derived from scratch by every successor. step 14 named that asymmetry; this step sets the ratio that corrects it. Measured the same day on the letter carrying this session: failures far outnumbered successes even though four sequences had WORKED -- a two-timestamp guard design with both commands verified, a leaf split that made a bug structurally impossible, a capture-policy promotion that built and passed, and a flag combination that cut a query from 1.650s to 0.882s. Only the failures felt obligatory to write, and a successor inheriting that ratio learns what to fear instead of what to do.

DECISION: WRITE TWICE AS MUCH SUCCESS AS FAILURE -- owner policy 2026-08-23, and it is a RATIO rather than an encouragement: for every failure recorded, TWO working procedures. WHEN: every knowledge-ification pass, and every moment a hard thing finally works. HOW: run wkappbot skill read knowledge-ification-procedure-jisikhwa-howto for the tagging convention, then tag the step VERIFIED or RESULT or DECISION and give it what step 11 demands, the paste-ready command plus the check that proved it, filed in the TASK skill where a working session meets it rather than in a reflection nobody opens mid-task. WHY: measured that day, the catalog held INCIDENT 155 against VERIFIED 49 among tagged steps, a 3.2-to-1 tilt toward failure, with 76.6 percent of all 4,067 steps carrying no tag at all. The tilt is STRUCTURAL and not laziness -- every guard mechanically DEMANDS a record when it refuses, and nothing anywhere demands one when something finally succeeds, so failures are conscripted into the catalog while successes must be volunteered. The cost falls hardest on the CHEAP tiers, which is the owner's real argument: an expensive model can re-derive a missing path, a cheap one cannot and will confidently report the path does not exist, measured the same day when a correctly-briefed sector claimed a broker division code was never used anywhere in a file while it sat twenty lines from where that sector had been reading. A catalog of failures teaches avoidance and never teaches the way through. SUPERSEDED AND SHARPENED 2026-08-31, owner ruling, and it replaces the ratio with a principle: a textbook contains no failure stories, because the lesson inside a failure is reachable only through direct experience -- for people as much as for models. A MILLION REMEMBERED FAILURE STORIES ARE WORTH LESS THAN ONE REMEMBERED SUCCESS STORY. So the default is now to write the working method and nothing else, and a failure record must EARN its place by a test it usually fails: would a reader who has not been told rebuild the broken thing, re-derive a measurement already taken, or walk into a trap no guard covers. Where a guard, a gate or a lock already blocks the failure, the mechanism carries it and the narrative is pure surplus. TIGHTENED 2026-09-08, owner ruling, and it closes the one loophole the earn-its-place test leaves open -- a failure narrative may NOT be MIGRATED into a skill. When a letter is trimmed to successes, the failure paragraphs are DROPPED, never relocated. A skill takes the RULE the failure produced, written in the imperative with no incident, no date and no actor, or it takes nothing. THE OPERATIONAL FORM, and it is what to do instead of reaching for the story: write the sequence that worked, in order, with the paste-ready command and the observable that proved it; where you want to warn against a route, describe the correct route in twice the detail instead, since a reader given a good path has no budget left for a bad one. THE EVIDENCE THAT SETTLED IT, kept to one line because the principle is the point: a session recorded a failure-mode rule and then committed that exact failure twenty minutes later, having read its own record -- which is the claim made concrete, that reading a failure teaches its shape and not its avoidance. Cross: harness-agent-brief-guard step 3 for the same rule applied to dispatch briefs.

DECISION: when a size gate measures a document, exempt the lines the harness REQUIRES and charge the lines an author chose. WHEN: you are writing any gate that refuses growth in a file which mixes mandatory declarations with discretionary prose -- CLAUDE.md being the sharpest case, where study-locks sit interleaved with commentary. HOW: wkappbot skill read claude-md-harness-rules for which lines are declarations, then filter those out of BOTH sides of the comparison before measuring, and say in the block message that the printed number is a measured size rather than the size on disk. WHY: designed 2026-09-06 for fat-md-growth. Registering a lock for a new module is work another gate DEMANDS, so measuring it would make one gate refuse what another requires and the pair would form a ring -- the shape this repo already recorded at descent, where the wish ratchet and the manifest checker read the same file for opposite evidence. Charging only the commentary also puts the pressure where the bloat actually accumulates, which is the narrated comment above a lock and not the lock.

THE CHEAPEST JISIKHWA IS EDITING THE REFUSAL, not writing another skill step -- put the knowledge where the reader is standing when it costs them. WHEN: a guard refuses you, you work out WHY, and the reason turns out to be absent from the refusal text itself. HOW: change the message, in the guard, in the same session, as a message-only edit touching no predicate, threshold or exemption -- then record in the related skill that you did, so the next session does not add the same sentence twice. WHY, measured 2026-09-07 on .githooks/lib/fat-md-growth.sh: that gate explained at length what MEASURED bytes excludes and that it fires only on growth, but never said what the growth was measured FROM. It is measured against HEAD, not the working copy, so a section inherited UNCOMMITTED from an earlier session is charged to whichever commit finally lands -- and a session that dutifully trims only its own new prose keeps being refused while the real weight sits in paragraphs it never wrote. That fact already existed as a skill step, in letter-edit, and it still cost a session two full rounds, because a skill is read BEFORE the work and a refusal is read DURING it. A GUARD THAT REFUSES CORRECTLY CAN STILL BE WRONG ABOUT WHY, and the reader pays that difference in whole rounds rather than in tokens. THE TEST for whether this applies: if you had to run an experiment to learn something the guard already knew, the guard owed you that sentence. THE LIMIT, so this does not become an excuse to grow every message: add only what the reader cannot derive from what is already printed, and never a narrative of how you found it -- one clause, indicative, no dates and no actors.

A TIER MOVE HAS A COMMAND -- USE --move-to INSTEAD OF RETYPING THE STEP INTO THE NEW HOME AND SHAVING THE OLD ONE. Measured 2026-09-11: the owner caught a SPEC filed into a -ref tier, and the repair was done by hand -- a fresh --add-step into the core, then a --find/--replace to hollow out the ref entry. That is two edits, two chances to paraphrase, and it leaves the old text subtly different from the new, which is precisely the drift the copy-then-delete rule exists to prevent. The sanctioned move lands the SAME BYTES in the new tier and removes them from the old in one operation, which is why it was built. WHEN: any time a step is in the wrong tier -- a spec or a TODO sitting in -ref, a work record sitting in a core, a procedure sitting anywhere but -howto. HOW: reach for the move first and keep the hand path as the fallback for the case a move cannot express, such as splitting one step into two homes; if you do fall back, copy VERBATIM and then delete by quote rather than rewriting from memory. THE DEEPER FINDING FROM THE SAME HOUR, and it is why the misfiling happened at all: the sell side had NO -howto tier, so every sell-side specification had nowhere legitimate to go and drifted into the core or the ref. A MISSING TIER IS A MISFILING GENERATOR -- when you catch a step in the wrong home, check whether its right home EXISTS before blaming the writer, and create the tier in the same breath. Cross-links: wkappbot skill read skill-contribute-edit for the edit commands, and wkappbot skill read harness-tier-score-guard for why an oversized core is what these moves relieve.

A FAILURE STORY IS MOVED AND THEN DELETED, TWO STEPS, and stopping after the first is how a catalogue silently doubles. Owner 2026-09-19, giving both the resolution and the reason. THE CONTRADICTION IT DISSOLVES: the operating file says failure narratives are deleted on sight and need no permission, while the edit guards make a raw delete hard and this catalogue forbids retyping a step by hand. His answer is that the -ref tier IS the work record, so a failure story landing there is being FILED rather than preserved as advice, which makes the move both the compliant act and the easy one with nothing to argue about. THE TIER ROLES HE RESTATED THE SAME NIGHT, sharper than the older wording: the CORE is reflexes, the -howto is SPEC plus TODO plus IMPLEMENTATION ORDER, the -ref is miscellany, and failure stories leave EVERY tier by default. PROOF THAT THE SECOND STEP GETS SKIPPED, measured minutes later inside this very skill: a move of a dated rename incident answered add-step skipped, identical step already exists at position 6, so an earlier pass had COPIED it to the ref and never removed the original, and every session since had read the same paragraph twice. THE CHECK, one command each way: after any move, grep the DESTINATION for the fragment and the SOURCE for its absence, then re-read the step count before claiming a skill got smaller, because the CLI can report a clean move while a post-hook says the write never landed. A REFINEMENT FROM THE SAME NIGHT: a step whose SUBJECT belongs to another skill goes to THAT skill rather than to the -ref -- a dispatcher-wrapper trap sitting inside a trading method was moved to codex-tool-wrappers, which lifts the source skill AND puts the knowledge where a reader would look, since -ref is this skill own history and never a bin for anything off topic. MEASURED PAYOFF, same sitting: two moves took this core from 22 steps and a blocked add to 20 steps at 100 of 100, so the healing and the unblocking are one act.

requirements.expect: a core of at most 10 steps ending in a NAVIGATION step that names BOTH satellites by id -- this is the shape a 3-tier split must produce, verified live 2026-07-15 when this exact skill was applied to a 13-step fat core that scored 0/100 and was blocking edits to tools/wkharness.ps1

an existing skill holding the PROCEDURES extracted from the fat core -- proves the -howto tier is a real created artifact, not advice; the harness score treats a satellite as the thing that lifts a core out of the sub-60 blocked band, so if this read fails the split did not happen
